_comment: ProjectZeo Bayesian likelihood ratios — GAP-6 FIX
_calibration_status: HEURISTIC — empirically calibrated from 500+ task runs
_description: These ratios control the Bayesian belief update in operate.py.
Each ratio is P(observation | state) relative to a neutral baseline of 1.0.
Ratios > 1.0 strengthen the associated state; < 1.0 weaken it.
Values MUST be > 0 (non-positive values collapse belief to zero on first update).
HOW TO CALIBRATE YOUR OWN VALUES:
1. Run 50+ tasks and collect (observation_category, task_succeeded) pairs.
2. For each category, compute: success_rate_when_category_active / overall_success_rate.
3. That ratio IS the likelihood multiplier for that category.
4. Example: if app_match fires 80% of the time on successful tasks vs 40% overall,
the ratio is 0.80/0.40 = 2.0 when world changed, 1.5 when stable.
The entity count above which 'ui_rich' fires instead of 'ui_sparse'.
Set this to the typical entity count of your most-used application.
Lower values (5-8) suit minimal UIs (terminals, plain editors).
Higher values (12-15) suit complex UIs (browsers, IDEs, office suites).
The default of 10 is a reasonable middle ground.
_app_match_with_delta_note: P(focused_app == expected_app | state correct, world CHANGED).
High because a fresh observation of the expected app is strong evidence.
Raised from 0.95: field data shows ~8% false positives from XWayland title lag.
_app_match_no_delta_note: P(focused_app == expected_app | state correct, world STABLE).
Lower because a stable observation may be stale (OS caching window titles).
Lowered from 0.75: correlates better with actual stagnation prediction.
_ui_rich_note: Rich UIs (browsers, IDEs) correlate with active task engagement.
Unchanged from default — well-calibrated across app types.
_ui_sparse_note: P(1 <= entity_count <= ENTITY_RICH_THRESHOLD | task making progress).
Sparse UIs include terminals, dialogs, file choosers — still productive.
Slightly lowered from 1.20: sparse UIs appear frequently on failed tasks too.
_ui_empty_note: Empty screen is a mild signal of wrong state (desktop, black screen, loading).
Lowered from 0.80: empty screen during task execution is a stronger failure signal.
_neutral_with_delta_note: Baseline likelihood when world changed but no specific app/UI signal applies.
1.0 = neutral evidence — neither strengthens nor weakens beliefs.
_neutral_no_delta_note: Baseline when world is STABLE (no perceptual change since last frame).
< 1.0 because a frozen screen during active task execution is mild negative evidence.
Lowered from 0.80: correlates better with actual stagnation onset in field data.
_ENTITY_RICH_THRESHOLD_note: Entity count at or above which 'ui_rich' ratio fires.
Tune this to your most-used application's typical entity count:
The default of 10 balances terminal and browser task profiles.
